title: Callimitra's skeleton is formed on the interfaces of a tetrahedral group of four cells

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Callimitra's skeleton is formed on the interfaces of a tetrahedral group of four cells

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The skeleton of the nassellarian Callimitra reproduces the interfacial film system of four soap-bubbles in tetrahedral contact (six plane interfaces meeting in threes at 120°, edges meeting near 109°), so it must have been formed at the interfaces of a tetrahedral group of cells.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: six plane interfaces meeting in threes at 120^\circ; edges meeting at \approx 109^\circ 28'

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It is obvious at a glance that this is such a skeleton as may have been formed (I think we may go so far as to say _must_ have been formed) at the interfaces of a little tetrahedral group of cells

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IX, “On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons”; topic “Nassellarian tetrahedral skeletons”. Scope: Nassellaria with tetrahedral skeletons (e.g. Callimitra)

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: six plane interfaces meeting in threes at 120^\circ; edges meeting at \approx 109^\circ 28'

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch09-16: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The geometry is precise, but mature shape alone cannot establish where it formed. The necessary developmental cellular context is too specialized to expect adequate public data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct Callimitra skeletons and developing cells in 3D, testing for six interfaces, triple junctions near 120 degrees and tetrahedral edge angles near 109.47 degrees with direct colocalization at cell boundaries. Development without four-cell contact would refute the asserted necessity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Modern developmental imaging of Callimitra is likely absent.

A tetrahedral skeleton can arise from non-cellular geometric processes.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.7
data existence: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.2

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The soap-film angles and the tetrahedral graph are specific enough to accept or reject from specimens or faithful images, and the claim is limited to a small group of nassellarians. Public images exist but quantitative 3D of Callimitra is thin, so the testable object is mostly the drawn or photographed geometry. That can confirm the geometric match for this genus and cannot establish the cellular history the geometry is said to require.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On Callimitra and similar nassellarian skeletons, count interfaces and measure meeting angles against Plateau's laws: faces in threes near 120 degrees and edges near the tetrahedral angle. Agreement supports a four-cell interfacial origin; angles far from those values, or a different topology, refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Many classical figures are schematic, and Haeckel-style drawings can impose the regularity being tested.

Angle agreement does not show that four living cells were present when the skeleton formed.
